title: Binary width bound
statement: Let $n,w$ be natural numbers and suppose $n<2^w$. Then the binary representation of $n$ has at most $w$ bits.
replaced: For all naturals $n$ and $w$ with $n < 2^w$, the binary representation of $n$ has at most $w$ bits, so one administrative increment is charged by two $w$-bit scans plus two transitions, with no unary representation of positions.
